scope: Desktop panel resizing now supports the W3C ARIA Window Splitter interaction pattern and reliably finishes pointer cancellation. The overall C acceptance remains OPEN.

source_control.runtime_message: fix(editor): make dock resizing keyboard accessible
source_control.push: Normal fast-forward push verified by git ls-remote and GitHub branch API. Runtime source, browser regression and cache-busted shell URL are in this commit.

implementation.behavior: Both desktop dock resize controls are focusable vertical role=separator widgets with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow and Hungarian aria-valuetext. Arrow keys resize 16 CSS px in the physical direction; Shift+Arrow resizes 48 px; Home/End choose the clamped minimum/maximum. RTL direction is respected.
implementation.persistence: Keyboard and pointer widths use the existing local shell state and opt into the existing custom layout; browser reload retains the width. Workspace profile application and reset synchronize the ARIA value with the rendered width.
implementation.pointer_lifecycle: Pointerup, pointercancel and lostpointercapture clean up listeners and interaction state. Pointer cancellation keeps the current partial width, updates ARIA and persists the local shell state.
implementation.mobile: Dock resizers remain hidden in the existing one-drawer mobile layout; no mobile drawer or touch target behavior changed.
implementation.source_license_review: The W3C WAI-ARIA APG Window Splitter pattern was fetched successfully (HTTP 200) and used as an accessibility behavior reference. The repository already uses a vanilla JavaScript shell; no third-party runtime code or dependency was necessary or imported.
